claim: Raptor says he is glad he wildcarded in gameweek 4 despite a poor points week, arguing his team value and points are up versus not wildcarding.
quote: But overall, very glad I wild carded.

claim: Raptor says Mendy suffered a suspected concussion and will likely miss gameweek 5, expected back for gameweek 6.
quote: Mendy by the way I think it was concussion so Mendy might be out and probably will be out for gameweek five

claim: Raptor plans to start Hall at home to Hull and bench Muharemović at home to Crystal Palace, waiting to see Monday night's Leeds-Newcastle game before deciding between them.
quote: let's see how Hall and Muerovic get on on Monday night

claim: Raptor considered starting Muharemović over Konsa given Arsenal's tough away trip to Brighton, but says he can't see himself benching his Arsenal defender.
quote: maybe I could be convinced throughout the week to start Muovic over Kzer

claim: Raptor will captain Haaland at home to Sunderland.
quote: Erling Harland as my captain against Sunderland at home

claim: Raptor says Szoboszlai plays an almost identical role to Groß, always on the pitch and on set pieces and penalties, but is 1.5m more expensive and calls picking him a mistake.
quote: he is Pascal Gross for me like almost identical so he is 1.5 million arguably overpriced

claim: Raptor's preferred single transfer is selling Szoboszlai for a high-upside player with good fixtures, naming Dewsbury-Hall as his first choice with Barnes or Elanga at Newcastle as alternatives.
quote: the only way I sell Soberly is if it's to move to a high upside asset that has really good fixtures like an Everton or Newcastle midfielder

claim: Raptor is weighing selling Rogers for Mbeumo or Gibbs-White but leans toward keeping Rogers since the options are closely matched, calling it an unnecessary transfer.
quote: selling Morgan Rogers to Brian and Burmo or Morgan Gibbs White

claim: Raptor's two-transfer option is Palmer to Fernandes funded by Ekitiké to Barry, but he says it's probably not worth two hits since he would not captain Fernandes anyway.
quote: Palmer to Fernandez and then I fund that by doing EAC to a cheap forward

claim: Raptor says Bournemouth are 12th for xG conceded and creating chances against, so he'll give Szoboszlai one more week there before possibly selling ahead of Liverpool's gameweek 6 trip to Man City.
quote: Bournemouth are 12th for XGC so far this season

claim: Raptor rates his gameweek 5 squad as good overall despite most players being away, and doesn't think one bad wildcard week justifies wholesale changes.
quote: It is a good team that you would still expect to do very well in gameweek five.

claim: Raptor says Ødegaard created six chances against Sunderland and was nearly on bonus points despite no attacking return, and plans to keep him for now.
quote: Erdigard created six chances in that game. Erdigard still is very nearly on bonus points in that game despite getting no attack in return

claim: Raptor says Isak was poor in gameweek 4 despite his brace, with only one real chance which he missed in the 93rd minute.
quote: he had one major chance which was actually in the 93rd minute and he missed it

claim: Raptor notes none of his three-plus penalty takers (Haaland, Palmer, Szoboszlai) won a penalty in gameweek 4, while Groß and Saka, whom he didn't own, both did.
quote: Harland Palmer Sol at the very least three pen takers. None of them got pens.

claim: Raptor does not rotate goalkeepers and will play Kinsky every week regardless of fixture.
quote: I don't have rotating goalkeepers, so it will save a lot of time in future content.

claim: Raptor recalls getting a big haul from an Arsenal-context defender he calls 'hinch' earlier in the season, using it as an example that lucky swings can go a manager's way too.
quote: I got like a hinch with 16 pointer in game one

claim: Raptor says Man City are second in the league for xG conceded this season, contrary to a narrative that their defense isn't good, factoring into a possible Liverpool front-two sale before GW6.
quote: They're sat second for XGC this season.

claim: Raptor says Fantasy Football Hub's team rater scores his gameweek 5 squad at 87%, which he attributes to having away fixtures for all but three players.
quote: This team is rated at 87% according to Fantasy Football Hub, which is pretty low.

claim: Raptor says it's worth banking free transfers into the three-week international break, since some nations play up to four times in the window.
quote: There's an international break coming up and it's a 3-w week international break where some nations play four times.

claim: Focal says Timber returned from injury for Arsenal, coming on for White, who then went off with a groin injury and is now a sell.
quote: Timber returned from injury last match. He came on for white. He had to go off of a groin injury.

claim: Focal says Timber could be a crazy differential if he's back and nailed on, but flags some risk this early in his return from injury.
quote: Timber could be a crazy differential if he is back and nailed on, but maybe a little bit risky so early on with his return

claim: Focal says O'Reilly was benched for Man City in the Manchester derby and now rates him a sell.
quote: But benched in the Manchester derby. So he's got to be a sell now.

claim: Focal says Mendy is unlikely to play gameweek 5 after a suspected concussion, and is top of the league for defensive contributions per 90 once his minutes return.
quote: he came off with a suspected concussion last game, so we won't see him next gimmick most likely

claim: Focal says Newcastle's and Everton's previous penalty takers have left the clubs, so it isn't certain Wissa stays on pens, with Garner floated as a possible Everton taker.
quote: we suspect Whistler and Barry going to be on pens but we don't know with 100% certainty

claim: Focal names Gibbs-White his number one target for gameweek 5 after an assist and max bonus against Villa, and says he understands the temptation to sell Szoboszlai to fund him.
quote: Gibbs White is the number one player I'd love to have this week.

claim: Focal calls Haaland the obvious captain choice for gameweek 5 at home to Sunderland, on four goals in four games.
quote: Harland top this week on seven points. The obvious captain choice.

claim: Focal advises holding transfers given the heavy midweek international schedule rather than moving early.
quote: hold your trifers if you can, but I know the temptation's there to go early

claim: Focal rates Wissa the top forward buy for gameweek 5 at home to Hull, who have now conceded six xG this season including two against Chelsea, ranking him just ahead of Barry.
quote: Whistler comes in as the second best forward this week. The perfect time to buy before playing whole home

claim: Focal says João Pedro was priced too cheap and is now the most-owned player in the game at roughly 75% ownership.
quote: he's about 75% owned. So three quarters of all teams have got Xiao Pedro, which is wild.

claim: Focal notes Saka's non-penalty xGI (2.5) is barely ahead of Ødegaard's (2.3) this season, suggesting Ødegaard could be the better long-term value once penalties are set aside.
quote: Saka's 2.5 nonpenex expected Golovven is barely ahead of Erdigard's 2.3 nonpenxgi this season

claim: Focal cites Mbeumo as the league's top midfielder for non-penalty xGI this season at 3.3, ahead of Bruno Fernandes on 2.6.
quote: bumo by the way is actually the top midfielder so far in the league for nonpenxgr with 3.3

claim: Focal says the top non-premium keepers through gameweek 30 are Verbruggen and Kinsky, both 4.5m, suggesting a 5m keeper isn't worth the extra spend.
quote: they're both 4.5 mil keepers. So, that does suggest that the 5 mil keeper is not worth it.

claim: Focal says Tarkowski is a strong buy at home to Ipswich, on 29 points in four gameweeks with two clean sheets, a goal and defensive-contribution returns.
quote: 29 points after four game weeks for Taroski as well. What a start.

claim: Focal says Groß is now FPL's top scoring player but is nowhere near his gameweek 5 buy list with Arsenal away next, relevant only as a bench option on a wildcard.
quote: It's Arsenal next for Brighton though, so their assets nowhere near the tables this week.

claim: Focal says Palace's Henderson is out injured and a Palace player was sent off, making Leeds' home fixture against them look good for Calvert-Lewin.
quote: given Henderson's out injured for Palace Dassi suspended with the red card, it does feel like a good game for Leads playing home

claim: Focal says Dewsbury-Hall looks like a great buy for his next two fixtures, and also works as a one-week pick for an international-break wildcard.
quote: Jewsbury Hall looks so good to buy this week as well for 6 mil those next two fixtures.

claim: Focal's projected team of the week for gameweek 5 is Donnarumma, Hall, Tarkowski, Thiaw, Bruno Fernandes, Dewsbury-Hall, Gibbs-White, Szoboszlai, Barry, Haaland and Wissa.

claim: Focal says Raya is now the top-scoring goalkeeper in the game after a clean sheet and penalty save worth 14 points.
quote: Ryer is now the top scoring keeper in the game after that clean sheet. Pen save 14 pointer.

claim: Focal says Verbruggen has been good but faces Arsenal next, so gameweek 5 is not the time to buy him.
quote: Now for Bugan does have Arsenal next so it's not the time to buy of course.
